## We compare businesses just below and above score 58. {#d2s2-p01 .reader-slide .s1-review .d2s2-review}

```{webr}
#| context: setup
#| autorun: true
#| echo: false
#| include: false
gw <- read.csv('evaluation_data_GreenWaste_simple.csv')
city <- subset(gw, setting == 'city')
near <- subset(city, abs(score - 58) <= 2)
near$below <- as.integer(near$score <= 58)
near$distance <- near$score - 58
```

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_plot())
```

**Efficiency score** is the running variable: it determines which side of **58** a business falls on. At or below 58 participated; above 58 did not.

::: {.ask}
Why compare businesses close to the score cut-off of 58?
:::

::: {.notes}
5 minutes. Orient from DiD to local post-period comparison. Programme remains equipment subsidies/help/training; outcome annual waste management cost 12 months after GreenWaste. Higher score means more efficient. Plot shows actual records scores53-63, shaded56-60. Full city10000; shaded545. Explain score, threshold, local comparison in that order. Proximity alone does not establish random assignment. Start webR warming. Q2/source page1 later links population. Transition: predict a fitted jump before lines appear.
:::

## What do you expect at score 58? {#d2s2-p02 .reader-slide .s1-review .d2s2-review}

::: {.ask}
Will fitted costs just below 58 be lower? Would the reduction reach 1,000 AED?
:::

<div data-choices><button data-choice aria-pressed="false">Little difference</button><button data-choice aria-pressed="false">At least 1,000 lower</button><button data-choice aria-pressed="false">Need evidence</button><p class="feedback" role="status"></p></div>

Give a reason before seeing the fitted lines. These buttons record a local choice; collect room responses with a show of hands.

::: {.notes}
4 minutes. One minute choose, two discuss reasons, one collect. Do not present cost patterns as proof of an effect. No fitted estimate revealed. Below-minus-above negative means lower cost. Transition: work with different small samples on either side.
:::

## What comparison should we make? {#d2s2-p03 .reader-slide .s1-review .d2s2-review}

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_plot())
```

Discuss with a partner. The shaded window contains **545 businesses with scores 56-60**.

::: {.ask}
Would comparing the average costs on each side tell us what happens at 58? What else could affect that gap?
:::

::: {.notes}
4 minutes. One minute inspect the plot, two discuss in pairs, one collect explanations. Each dot is a business; blue is at or below 58, grey is above. Shading marks the two-point window. A raw mean gap also reflects where the businesses sit along the score scale and variation in costs. It does not isolate the fitted comparison at 58 or establish an effect. No cards, arithmetic or number-line poster are needed. Q1 on worksheet page 3 records the same reasoning. Transition: compare fitted costs as the score approaches 58 from each side.
:::

## Compare businesses at the same score. {#d2s2-p04 .reader-slide .s1-review .d2s2-review}

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_plot(fit=TRUE, jump=FALSE, steps=TRUE))
```

The two lines allow costs to slope differently on each side. Follow each line towards **58**.

::: {.ask}
Why might the gap between group averages differ from the gap where these lines reach 58?
:::

::: {.notes}
4 minutes. Advance once to reveal the participating-side line, then again for the comparison-side line. Each uses businesses in the shaded window. Ask the room to follow both to 58 before describing the gap. We compare fitted limits at the same cut-off, rather than averages over different scores. There need not be a business observed exactly at 58. Keep the jump and number withheld until the next slide. Complete Q1 on worksheet page 3. Transition: identify and interpret the vertical gap.
:::

## Read the jump at 58. {#d2s2-p05 .reader-slide .s1-review .d2s2-review}

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_plot(fit=TRUE))
```

::: {.ask}
The fitted jump is **-721 AED**. Explain the comparison, sign and units to your partner.
:::

This uses **545 businesses**. Negative means lower annual waste costs on the participating side, measured **12 months after GreenWaste**.

::: {.notes}
4 minutes. Point out the red vertical gap between the two fitted limits at 58. Give pairs two minutes to explain it, then hear and refine one interpretation: fitted annual waste cost immediately on the participating side is 721 AED lower than on the comparison side. This is a local comparison, not a citywide average. A causal reading still requires a credible design; the checks come later. Q2 on worksheet page 3 uses the reference figure on page 2. Transition: find the same jump, sample and interval in the regression table.
:::

## We fit the two local slopes in R. {#d2s2-p07 .reader-slide .s1-review .d2s2-review}

```{webr}
#| echo: true
# Compare waste cost 12 months after GreenWaste, within two points of score 58.
# Allow a different cost slope on each side of the cut-off.
fit <- lm(cost_after ~ below * distance, data = near)
# Report the fitted jump at 58, in whole AED.
round(coef(fit)['below'])
```

::: {.ask}
Does this calculate the average gap across the window, or a fitted gap at the cut-off?
:::

Paper result: **-721 AED**. Participants do not need to write or run R.

::: {.notes}
5 minutes. Predictthenone trainerRun. OLScoefficientidenticaltorobustcoefficient; displayedCIcomesHC2estimatr, notdefaultlmCI. Codecommentsdescribeunits/window/slopes/output. Noparticipantcoding. If delayedusepaperresultsame time. Transition: evaluatorchooseswindow; ask sensitivity.
:::

## Which check would change your advice? {#d2s2-p15 .reader-slide .s1-review .d2s2-review}

Keep **H5-A open**. Close AI responses and peer comments.

::: {.ask}
Write one local-result interpretation and one specific evidence request. How could the answer change your advice?
:::

Use the **final box on worksheet page 4**.

Next: finding comparisons with similar recorded characteristics.

::: {.notes}
6 minutes. Three independent, one pair purpose check, two feedback. Require a local fitted comparison at 58, units, conditional causal reading and threshold limit. Request score setting/influence, the age jump/other predetermined checks, the window or transportability, with a reason. Do not claim the cut-off is a lottery or representative. Total 80 minutes. Use this teaching source with its matching six-page worksheet; the visual pair discussion requires no group cards.
:::
